_comment: Data for `discover-queries`. {topic} is replaced by the user's topic. Queries are web-search strings, not scraping targets: open only public pages and respect each site's robots/ToS.

marketplaces.name: CodeCanyon (Envato Market)
marketplaces.demo_hints: Item pages have a 'Live Preview' button (often a frame or an external demo URL). Demo logins, when published, are usually in the item description or in the live-preview toolbar, not in the preview itself.
marketplaces.notes: Public item pages only. Purchasing, downloading code and logging in to Envato accounts are out of scope.

marketplaces.name: ThemeForest (Envato Market)
marketplaces.demo_hints: Mostly front-end themes and admin templates. Previews show screens but often have no backend; treat them as UI references and say so.
marketplaces.notes: Public item pages only. Themes rarely contain real workflows; record that limitation.

marketplaces.name: Envato Elements
marketplaces.demo_hints: Asset library with static previews; no application demos or demo logins in general.
marketplaces.notes: Low value for application research. Include only when the user asks for visual templates.

marketplaces.name: GitHub (open-source catalogue)
query_templates: "{topic}" self-hosted open source demo site github
marketplaces.demo_hints: READMEs often link a hosted demo and list a demo account. Prefer the project's own README or docs site over forks.
marketplaces.notes: Only credentials the maintainers state for a public demo count. Do not search commit history, issues or config files for secrets.

marketplaces.name: SourceForge
marketplaces.demo_hints: Project pages sometimes link a demo site or a hosted sandbox.
marketplaces.notes: Many entries are inactive; check last-update dates.

marketplaces.name: Product Hunt
marketplaces.demo_hints: Launch pages link to the vendor site; follow the link and use the vendor's own demo/trial page.
marketplaces.notes: Discovery only. Verify claims on the vendor's own site.

marketplaces.name: AlternativeTo
marketplaces.demo_hints: Lists competitors and licence type (open source, free, paid). Use it to widen the candidate list, then go to vendor sites.
marketplaces.notes: Community-edited; treat as a lead, not as evidence.

marketplaces.name: G2
marketplaces.demo_hints: Category pages rank products and show whether a free trial or demo exists. Follow through to the vendor.
marketplaces.notes: Review pages can block automated access; use search results and the vendor site, do not scrape.

marketplaces.name: Capterra
marketplaces.demo_hints: Listings flag 'Free trial' / 'Free version' and link to the vendor.
marketplaces.notes: Same as G2: leads only; verify on the vendor's own pages.

marketplaces.name: Odoo Apps
marketplaces.demo_hints: Odoo itself offers a free trial instance after registration; app pages may link a vendor demo. Registration-only access is recorded as registration_required.
marketplaces.notes: Do not create accounts unless the user asked and supplied the details.

marketplaces.name: WordPress plugin directory
marketplaces.demo_hints: Plugin pages have a 'Preview' button for the WordPress Playground in some cases and vendor demo links in the description.
marketplaces.notes: Free-plugin demos are often a disposable sandbox; record that in notes.

marketplaces.name: Shopify App Store
marketplaces.demo_hints: Listings often link a demo store or video. Real use needs a Shopify store; record as registration_required.
marketplaces.notes: Do not install apps on stores you do not own.

marketplaces.name: AppSumo
marketplaces.demo_hints: Deal pages link to the vendor and sometimes a demo video or public demo account.
marketplaces.notes: Discovery only; purchasing is out of scope.

marketplaces.name: Vendor sites (generic demo search)
marketplaces.demo_hints: Look for the vendor's own demo/pricing/docs pages that state credentials in text on a public page.
marketplaces.notes: Ignore pastebins, forums of leaked data and credential lists. Only vendor- or marketplace-published demo credentials count.
